stem:
The figure shows a cell, a buzzer, and a switch S. The switch is closed, so its contacts touch.

Is the circuit ON or OFF?

options.text: ON — the closed switch completes the path, so current can flow.
OFF — a closed switch always stops current.
OFF — the buzzer blocks the cell even when the switch is closed.
ON — only because the switch itself supplies current to the buzzer.

teacher.key_rationale: When switch contacts touch, the path is complete, so the circuit is ON and current can flow. Claiming a closed switch stops current, that the buzzer blocks the cell, or that the switch supplies current are wrong about the same ON/OFF idea.
teacher.figure_note: Cell, buzzer, and closed switch S forming a complete loop.
